content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1 (Maximum no-overtime recovery) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best available plan but only reaches 64.3% service level against the 80% target for 14:45-16:45.","why":"The gap is caused by the card authorisation gateway outage (P1 opened 12:37), not missing staff. Payments calls hit 240 against 108 forecast, and card_declined calls are running at 2.48x normal. R1 combines delayed breaks, cancelled coaching, IVR outage messaging, chat deflection on both queues, payments callback, and moving 4 cross-skilled agents to payments from 16:00. It is predicted to lift the window from 48.2% (no action) to 64.3%, cut abandons from 13.4% to 9.1%, and bring rest-of-day to 79.9%, at an extra cost of INR 2,358. No plan reaches 80%. Escalation is flagged (ESC-02) because even the best compliant plan is below the 70% escalation line. The duty manager should decide whether further measures are warranted while the outage continues, such as overtime or wider customer messaging.","trade_offs":["Cost: R1 is the most expensive option at INR 2,358, versus INR 2,070 for R2 (62.7%) and INR 1,485 for P3 (60.4%). The extra spend buys about 1.6 to 3.9 points.","Payments queue: R1 predicts payments at 54.0%, slightly below P3 (55.2%). Its overall gain comes mostly from general rising to 84.6%, so payments customers still face long waits.","Customer impact: R1 uses the most customer-facing changes, including the IVR outage message, chat deflection on both queues and callbacks. P4 avoids these entirely but only reaches 56.5%.","Other queue: moving 4 agents from general is offset by general-side chat deflection, so general is not hurt. It stays at 84.6%, versus 66.4% with no action."],"watch":"Track payments service level and card_declined volumes each interval, and watch for any update on when the gateway will be restored. If the outage runs past 16:45 or payments stays near 54%, escalate further with the duty manager. Also check general is holding up after the 4-agent move at 16:00."}
